newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ADAMS NO LONGER LIVING A LIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ADAMS NO LONGER LIVING A LIE.

text.p: Former England soccer captain Tony Adams on Saturday admitted he was an alcoholic and said he would concentrate on himself in his battle for recovery.
The lanky Arsenal defender said he was attending meetings of Alcoholics Anonymous in a bid to end his long-standing problems with drink.

"I think I will be better for it and that's bigger than football, bigger than my family, bigger than everything. It's me now and it's all about me," he told a crowd of reporters outside Arsenal's training ground.
"I don't want to cure anyone else, I want to cure myself."
Adams, 29, said the turning point came when he looked at himself in the mirror.
"I'm not living a lie anymore, which is great. I feel a lot better for it," he said.

"It's not just happened. It's been a long time and I'm on the road to recovery now. It's not just happened overnight, I'd like to make that point clear...I've been attending Alcoholics Anonymous and it's okay. I'm on the road to recovery."

Adams, who twice won the English league championship with his club, said it had been immensely hard to break the news to his team mates on Friday but praised striker Paul Merson, who has also fought a high-profile battle against gambling, drink and drug addiction.
"Paul's been fantastic for me, obviously he understands me, he knows what I'm going through and he's been there for me," said Adams.
"I'm changing my life. and I'd like the respect now, from you...No, I want the respect from myself, actually. I've got a lot of things to do, a lot of things to work on myself and I'm doing it."
